children: (“Afya” or the “Company”), the leading medical education group and medical practice solutions provider in Brazil, reported today its financial and operating results for the three and nine-month period, which ended September 30, 2026 (third quarter 2026). Financial results are expressed in Brazilian Reais and are presented in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”).

These materials are not an offer for sale of securities in the United States, nor a solicitation of votes or proxies. The securities have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and may not be offered or sold in the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, any U.S. person absent registration or an exemption from registration under the Securities Act. The issuer does not intend to register any part of the offering in the United States or to conduct a public offering of securities in the United States.
3Q26 Revenue increased 6.1% YoY to R$985.2 million.
3Q26 Adjusted EBITDA increased 8.7% YoY to R$433.8 million, with an Adjusted EBITDA Margin of 44.0%, an increase of 100 bps YoY.
3Q26 Net Income increased 7.2% YoY to R$171.0 million. Basic EPS increased 10.0% YoY to R$1.88.
9M26 Revenue increased 6.7% YoY to R$2,970.0 million. Revenue excluding acquisitions increased 6.4%, reaching R$2,962.8 million.

9M26 Adjusted EBITDA increased 4.6% YoY reaching R$1,351.8 million, with an Adjusted EBITDA Margin of 45.5%. Adjusted EBITDA Margin decreased 90 bps YoY. Adjusted EBITDA excluding acquisitions grew 4.5%, reaching R$1,349.6 million, with an Adjusted EBITDA Margin of 45.6%.
9M26 Net Income increased 6.9% YoY to R$634.0 million. Basic EPS increased 9.1% YoY to R$6.98.
Operating Cash Conversion Ratio reached 99.5%, with Cash Flow from Operating Activities of R$1,332.7 million and Cash and Cash Equivalents of R$1,288.9 million.
Free Cash Flow to Equity reached R$629.0 million in 9M26, of which R$205.6 million was generated in the third quarter.

Afya closed the third quarter of 2026 with solid financial and operating results, supported by the continued strength of our Medical Education business. Revenue increased 6.1% year over year to R$985.2 million, while Adjusted EBITDA increased 8.7% to R$433.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA Margin reached 44.0%, up 100 basis points from the same period last year.

For the nine months of 2026, Revenue reached R$2,970.0 million, up 6.7% year over year. Adjusted EBITDA reached R$1,351.8 million, up 4.6%, with an Adjusted EBITDA Margin of 45.5%. Net Income increased 6.9% to R$634.0 million, while Basic EPS increased 9.1% to R$6.98.

Undergraduate remained the main driver of our performance. We concluded another successful intake cycle, maintaining full occupancy across our Medical School programs. The continued maturation of our medical school seats, the increase in the Medical School net average ticket, and the expansion of the average student base in Health Sciences and other undergraduate programs supported the growth delivered in the nine months of the year. Following the authorization of 17 additional seats at Afya Cruzeiro do Sul, our total approved medical school seats reached 3,785.

Academic excellence remains at the core of our Medical Education strategy. We currently have nine Medical Schools accredited by SAEME-CFM, providing independent external validation of the quality of our medical programs. Recognized by the World Federation for Medical Education, SAEME-CFM reinforces our commitment to academic excellence and continuous improvement across our network.

We also continued to advance our ESG performance, with our MSCI ESG Rating improving from BBB to AA. This progress resulted in Afya being recognized for the first time as an ESG Leader within the Diversified Consumer Services industry and positioned us as the highest-rated education company in Latin America.

Continuing Education ended the quarter with over 55 thousand students, up 10.0% year over year, supported by growth in the Graduate Journey and Other Courses even with lower B2B revenue. In Medical Practice Solutions, active payers increased 2.2% year over year to 206 thousand. Revenue in both segments remained broadly stable in the first nine months of 2026 as we continued to invest in scalable platforms and deeper engagement across the physician journey.

Cash generation remained strong. Cash Flow from Operating Activities reached R$1,332.7 million in the nine months of 2026, with an Operating Cash Conversion Ratio of 99.5%. We ended September with Cash and Cash Equivalents of R$1,288.9 million and Net Debt, excluding the effect of IFRS 16, of R$1,199.8 million, down R$169.7 million from December 31, 2025. During the period, we returned R$459.3 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases while continuing to reduce Net Debt. Based on the midpoint of our 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance, Net Debt excluding IFRS 16 represented approximately 0.7 times Adjusted EBITDA.
On September 23, 2026, Afya entered into a binding merger agreement with Yduqs, bringing together two complementary education platforms. Under the terms of the agreement,

each Class A and Class B common share of the Company would be converted into the right to receive common shares issued by Yduqs, such that, at closing, the Company’s shareholders and Yduqs shareholders would hold 69.0% and 31.0%, respectively, of the Combined Company on a fully diluted basis. The proposed transaction remains subject to
approval by Afya's and Yduqs' shareholders, antitrust and other customary approvals and closing conditions. Afya and Yduqs will continue to operate independently until completion.

On Afya Day 2026, we reinforced the strategic priorities that will guide the next phase of our growth. Our Medical Education business remains the foundation of our model, while Continuing Education and Medical Practice Solutions expand our relationship with physicians throughout their professional journey. We also presented how technology, data and artificial intelligence can support more personalized learning experiences, increase engagement and enhance the solutions offered across our physician-centric ecosystem.

As we enter the final quarter of 2026, we remain focused on the consistent execution of our strategy, operational efficiency, cash generation and disciplined capital allocation. Supported by the performance delivered in the nine months of the year and the resilience of our business model, we reaffirm our Full-Year 2026 Guidance.

On September 18, 2026, the Company announced that the Secretary of Regulation and Supervision of Higher Education of the Ministry of Education (“MEC”) authorized the increase of 17 medical seats of ITPAC Cruzeiro do Sul – Instituto Tocantinense Presidente Antonio Carlos Porto S.A. (“AFYA Cruzeiro do Sul”), in the city of Cruzeiro do Sul, located in the state of Acre. With the authorization, Afya reaches 67 medical seats on this campus, bringing the total approved seats to 3,785. This significant presence underscores our commitment to providing quality medical education and our role as Brazil’s leading provider of medical education.

On September 23, 2026, the Company announced that it had entered into a merger agreement with Yduqs Participações S.A. (“Yduqs”), establishing the terms and conditions for the business combination of the two companies.

Under the terms of the agreement, the Company would merge into Yduqs, with Yduqs continuing as the surviving entity (the “Combined Company”) and becoming the holding company for the combined group. Upon completion of the Proposed Transaction, the common shares of the Combined Company would continue to be listed solely on B3 S.A. – Brasil, Bolsa, Balcão, under the Novo Mercado segment.

Each Class A and Class B common share of the Company would be cancelled and cease to exist and, except for certain exclusions, and subject to the treatment of Ineligible Shareholders (as defined below), would represent solely the right to receive common shares issued by the Combined Company, such that, at closing, the Company’s shareholders and Yduqs’s shareholders would hold 69.0% and 31.0%, respectively, of the Combined Company on a fully diluted basis. As of the signing date, the exchange ratio represented 6.408347 Yduqs shares for each share of the Company.

In addition, certain significant shareholders of the Company and Yduqs entered into a voting commitment agreement pursuant to which they agreed to vote their shares in favor of the Proposed Transaction, subject to the terms and conditions set forth therein.

The consummation of the Proposed Transaction is subject to the satisfaction of certain customary conditions precedent for transactions of this nature, including, among others, approval by the shareholders of both companies, approval by the relevant antitrust authorities, the obtaining of certain third-party consents, the absence of any material adverse effect, and the satisfaction of other closing conditions set forth in the agreement. The contractual deadline for consummation of the Proposed Transaction is March 31, 2028, subject to the extension provisions set forth in the agreement.

Eligibility

The common shares of the Combined Company to be delivered in the merger have not been and will not be registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and will be delivered only in transactions exempt from, or not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act or the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended.

Accordingly, and as more fully described in the transaction documents to be made available to shareholders:

Eligible shareholders. Afya shareholders who (i) deliver a valid certification, in accordance with procedures to be established by Afya and Yduqs (an “Eligibility Certification”), that they are a qualified institutional buyer as defined in Rule 144A under the Securities Act (a “QIB”), an institutional accredited investor as defined in Rule 501(a) under the Securities Act (an “institutional accredited investor”), or a non-U.S. person within the meaning of Regulation S under the Securities Act (a “non-U.S. person”), or (ii) are persons to whom an offer of common shares of the Combined Company can otherwise be made pursuant to an available exemption from registration under the Securities Act (together, “Eligible Shareholders”), will be entitled to receive common shares of the Combined Company as merger consideration.

Ineligible shareholders. Afya shareholders that are not Eligible Shareholders (“Ineligible Shareholders”) will not receive common shares of the Combined Company. Instead, the common shares of the Combined Company that would otherwise have been issued to those Ineligible Shareholders are expected to be sold following closing on the B3 by a broker or other agent designated by mutual agreement of Afya and Yduqs, and the net cash proceeds of those sales are expected to be distributed to the Ineligible Shareholders. Neither Afya nor Yduqs makes any representation as to the amount or timing of any net cash proceeds that may be distributed under these mechanics, which will depend on market prices for the common shares of the Combined Company on the B3 at the time of sale, applicable costs and taxes, and prevailing exchange rates. As a matter of Cayman Islands law, every holder of record of Afya common shares on the record date is entitled to attend and vote at the meeting of shareholders to resolve on the Proposed Transaction. In order to comply with U.S. securities laws, Afya is not soliciting votes or proxies from Ineligible Shareholders.

This release is not an offer of securities in the United States or a solicitation of votes or proxies, in the United States or to any person who has not satisfied applicable eligibility conditions. Only Afya shareholders who (i) deliver a valid certification that they are a QIB, an institutional accredited investor, or a non-U.S. person, or (ii) are persons to whom an offer of common shares of the Combined Company can otherwise be made pursuant to an available exemption from registration under the Securities Act, will be entitled to receive common shares of the Combined Company as merger consideration. U.S. persons who are not QIBs, institutional accredited investors or persons to whom an offer can otherwise be made pursuant to an exemption from the registration requirements of the Securities Act are expected instead to receive net cash proceeds from a post-closing sale process.

Revenue totaled R$985.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, increasing 6.1% year over year. For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, Revenue totaled R$2,970.0 million, up 6.7% year over year. Excluding acquisitions, Revenue reached R$2,962.8 million, representing 6.4% organic growth.

Revenue growth in the nine months of 2026 was driven by the continued strength of our Medical Schools, supported by a 3.9% increase in medical school’s net average ticket, the expansion of the average student base in Health Sciences by 18.0% and in other undergraduate programs by 10.6%. Together, these drivers contributed to organic Revenue growth of 6.4% year over year.

Adjusted EBITDA reached R$433.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 8.7% year over year, while Adjusted EBITDA Margin was 44.0%, up 100 basis points from the prior-year period. The margin expansion was primarily driven by higher gross margins in the Undergraduate segment and partially offset by gross margin compression in the Continuing Education and Medical Practice Solutions segments.

For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, Adjusted EBITDA totaled R$1,351.8 million, up 4.6% year over year, with an Adjusted EBITDA Margin of 45.5%, down 90 basis points. The decrease in Adjusted EBITDA Margin was primarily driven by lower gross margins in Continuing Education and Medical Practice Solutions associated with the ongoing investment cycle in both segments and higher sales and marketing expenses.

Net Income for the third quarter of 2026 totaled R$171.0 million, up 7.2% year over year. For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, Net Income reached R$634.0 million, up 6.9% from the same period of 2025. The increase in the quarter mainly reflects operating performance partially offset by higher net finance expenses and income tax expenses. For the nine-month period, the increase reflects continued operating performance and a tax impact resulting from the implementation of the OECD Pillar Two rules in Brazil.

Basic EPS reached R$ 1.88 for the third quarter of 2026, up 10.0% year over year, and R$ 6.98 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, up 9.1% YoY. The higher growth in Basic EPS compared to Net Income reflects the impact of the Company's share repurchase program.

To supplement the Company's consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with IFRS accounting standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board—IASB, Afya presents Adjusted EBITDA and Operating Cash Conversion Ratio which are non-GAAP financial measures, for the convenience of investors. A non-GAAP financial measure is generally defined as one that intends to measure financial performance but excludes or includes amounts that would not be equally adjusted in the most comparable GAAP measure.

Afya calculates Adjusted EBITDA as net income plus/minus net financial result, plus income taxes expense, plus depreciation and amortization, plus interest received on late payments of monthly tuition fees, plus share-based compensation, plus/minus income share associate, plus/minus non-recurring expenses/income. Operating Cash Conversion Ratio is calculated as the Cash flow from Operating Activities plus income taxes paid, minus/plus non-recurring expenses/income divided by Adjusted EBITDA.

Free Cash Flow to Equity is calculated as the change in Net Debt ex-IFRS 16 between the beginning of the current period and the end of the current period, plus cash paid for acquisitions of subsidiaries or business combinations, plus dividends paid to the Company's shareholders, plus cash used in treasury share repurchases.

The non-GAAP supplemental financial measures are provided with the intend to help investors in assessing the overall performance of Afya’s business regarding its core operations, cash generation and profitability. The non-GAAP financial measures described in this release are not substitutes for the IFRS measures. In addition, the calculations of Adjusted EBITDA and Operating Cash Conversion Ratio are not standardized financial measures and may differ from the calculations used by other companies, including competitors in the education services industry, and therefore, Afya’s measures may not be comparable to those of other companies.
